subject: Console slice attribution UX + missed-SLO fallback mapping
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Slice attribution UI + missed-SLO fallback — urgent ask

Olga / Soojin,

Quick context: Acme reported a customer-visible slow-down last week that ended up being a missed SLO for one of their high-traffic tenants. They were able to route around it manually, but asked for two things in the console:

1) A clear per-slice attribution card (cost + P95 latency + error rate) that maps to tenant and route names shown in billing.
2) A visible mapping of our SLO fallback policies (what model/region we fail to and expected latency delta) next to the route tile — customers want to see what fallback will kick in.

We need a cross-functional quick-win that we can ship in the next sprint (2 weeks) and a follow-up roadmap item for a full UX that supports tenant-level filters.

Asks:
- Soojin: can we surface the current mapping data (route -> fallback model + region + expected latency delta) from telemetry? How brittle is the mapping today?
- Olga: can you own a short mock and a rollout plan (canary -> all) and coordinate with CS for messaging?
- Priya: prioritization guidance — is this sprint-level or next sprint?

I copied the Acme contact below so we can keep them in the loop. Attaching an initial sketch of the card I built in Figma.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Console Product
Redwood Inference
attachments: slice-attribution-mockup.png (image/png)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Slice attribution UI + missed-SLO fallback — urgent ask

Thanks Marissa — flagged. Short answers up front:
- We already compute fallback mappings as part of routing logic (model variant + region + reason). That data is in the routing audit log but not indexed in the metrics DB in a way the Console can query cheaply.
- Cost + P95 + errors per slice are available but at different keys; we have a materialized view we can use, but it needs a small transform to match billing identifiers (tenant_id -> account_display_name).

Constraints and options:
- Option A (fast): expose a cached index endpoint that joins routing-audit -> metric-slate -> billing-names. This would take ~4 dev days to wire and 1 day for a simple UI tile.
- Option B (longer but better): add the join at ingestion so the Console can query arbitrarily. This is 3 weeks of infra work.

I think Option A gets the ask done in 2 weeks and supports a canary. I'll validate the expected latency delta numbers (we sample fallback latencies today, need to expand sample rate to avoid noisy deltas).

I'll also drop a short spec for the endpoint and required fields.

-On Soojin

We should treat this as high priority for two reasons:
- It's a directly observable stickiness/leak risk for a top-20 account (Acme is at risk of moving workloads if they can't triage).
- It also maps to a number of CS tickets asking for more transparency.

Priya's ask: ship Option A as a short-term fix in the next sprint (two weeks). Parade of follow-ups:
- Add tenant filters and download CSV in the follow-up UX (roadmap).
- Instrument fallback latency sampling to reduce noise (Soojin owns).
- CS to prepare canned messaging and incident summary (Marissa owns).

If this is a go, we should put a canary on Acme's tenant for a week and collect feedback.

Priya

Subject: Re: Slice attribution UI + missed-SLO fallback — Acme impact note

Hi Marissa / Olga,

Thanks for the quick attention. For context from our side:
- The incident impacted roughly 6% of our traffic to the inference route used by our recommendations product; we saw P95 jump from 280ms to 980ms during the fallback window.
- Our engineers had to manually exclude a tenant slice and re-route requests to a different pool to bring latency back down. That workaround is not something we want to do regularly.

If you can show the fallback mapping and an expected latency delta in the Console, that'll let our on-call teams triage faster and decide whether to opt into automatic fallbacks for specific tenants.

Happy to be part of the canary and give feedback on the mock.

Best,
Elena
Platform Lead, Acme AI
